def.name: blockout-nave
def.description: Grey construction massing for a 12 x 24 m nave with a steep roof.

def.name: blockout-tower
def.description: Grey construction massing for a 4 m square tower.

steps.label: shell: church walls, roof and forecourt
west front: towers, portal and gable

def.name: black-church-tower
def.description: A black stone Gothic bell tower (4 m square, 19.7 m) with corner buttresses, louvred belfry lancets, four green corner pinnacles and a tall green octagonal spire with a gold cross (36 m overall).

def.name: black-church-portal
def.description: A Gothic west front for the black church: a deep pointed portal (clustered black piers, three archivolts, a glowing trefoil tympanum, a steep gable with green pinnacles) framing the open front doors, and a stained-glass rose window above. Only the two piers are solid; the 2.7 m opening between them stays clear.

def.name: black-church-west-gable
def.description: The west gable dressing of the black church: black raking copings and kneelers, and a slender green flèche with a lit lantern and a gold cross rising from the west end of the ridge. Decorative, never collides.

def.name: black-church-buttress
def.description: A stepped black stone buttress (1 × 1.5 m, 5.9 m) topped by a small green pinnacle; stands flush against a wall.

def.name: black-church-lancet
def.description: A tall Gothic lancet window (1.1 m wide, 1.2 to 4.4 m) of glowing stained glass in black tracery, made to sit flush on an exterior wall; decorative, never collides.

def.name: black-church-coping
def.description: Black raking copings for a 12 m church gable (58 degree pitch) with kneelers and a green apex finial; decorative, never collides.
